newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dodgers talk, EchoStar woes depress News.
newsitem.headline: Dodgers talk, EchoStar woes depress News.

text.p: Shares in Rupert Murdoch-controlled media giant News Corporation Ltd dived to their lowest level in a month on Wednesday as traders sold down on concerns over its Echostar situation and talk of further acquisitions in the U.S.
By 11.20 a.m. (0120 GMT), News Corp shares were 18 cents or over three percent lower at A$5.75. This followed a two percent fall in the company's ADRs in U.S. trade on Tuesday.
"Echostar was not good news for the stock and people don't like the possibility of them buying the Dodgers," said a dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.
News faces legal action in the U.S. from its would-be satellite partner EchoStar Communications Corp as the US$1 billion deal the two companies signed in February appeared to unravel.
News said on May 12 it would contest the claim in court with a spokesman adding the chances of the deal being kept alive were "very unlikely".

Talk of further spending by the acquisitive media mogul also dampened shares with reports from the U.S. that News division, Fox Sports, was looking to buy the Los Angeles Dodgers baseball team for over US$350 million.
By 11.30 a.m. (0130 GMT), News shares were 17 cents lower at A$5.76 on turnover of 2.07 million shares.
